messages:
Aisha: Heads-up — canary (model-v2) on staging showed a big KV miss-rate spike and sticky-session bleed into baseline earlier. We aborted, but we need a concise rollback playbook for prod that covers: immediate fast-switchback, safe session drain, targeted KV eviction (no herd), and temporary quota guards. Who can own ops steps?
Tom: +1. Proposed quick plan: 0) set traffic-split to 0 for canary, 1) flip stickiness off for routing rule, 2) set conservative quota for canary pool, 3) purge keys with rolling batches, 4) drain existing sessions.
Morgan: For stickiness, set the routing rule property: `"stickiness": false`. Existing sticky cookies can be expired server-side with a Set-Cookie response: `Set-Cookie: session_sticky=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; Domain=.ourdomain.com` — use for 2-3 request cycles.
Kevin: KV eviction command I ran on staging (example):
```
infractl kv purge --prefix "model-v2-session:" --batch-size 1000 --rate 50/s --dry-run
```
Remove --dry-run when ready. Important: do prefix-scoped purges, and add a 30s sleep between batches to avoid traffic spikes.
Eli: Quota guard: temporarily patch canary pool throttle to 10rps and small burst to limit regen pressure. Example API: 
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://api.redwood.local/config/pools/canary-1 -d '{"rate_limit":{"rps":10,"burst":20}}'
```
This prevents token-bucket refills from overwhelming dependent caches.
ops-bot: Alert: canary rollback requested by Aisha. Job queued: rollback-1768501234. Notify channel #eng-oncall if production.
Tom: For the fast switch: recommended console path -> Routing > Traffic Splits > select canary-1 -> set split = 0 and hit Save. API equivalent: 
```json
PATCH /routing/traffic-splits/12345
{ "splits": [{"pool":"baseline","pct":100}]}
```
Morgan: Drain sessions gracefully: hit admin drain endpoint on canary instances: `POST /admin/drain?mode=soft&timeout=300` — that'll stop new sessions but continue to serve active ones for up to 5m. After drain, do small-scale key purge of session prefixes.
Kevin: Important KV note: if you purge keys cold, downstream requests will repopulate cache; to avoid jetting load to baseline, do staggered purge + enable short-lived prefix TTL for 1 hour: `kvctl set-ttl --prefix model-v2-session: --ttl 3600` then run purge batches.
Eli: Also add an emergency routing guard: `no-new-sessions=true` tag on canary, checked by router at accept time. Quick toggle via API: `POST /ops/flags?no-new-sessions=canary-1:on`.
Aisha: Ownership — Tom execute traffic switch (0-2m), Eli apply quota & flag (2-4m), Kevin kick off staged KV purge (4-20m), Morgan handle cookie expiry and session drain (2-10m). I will notify support and oncall and watch metrics (latency, KV miss-rate, 50/95/99p).
Tom: One more safety: set a temporary route fallback for model-v2 to a smaller model variant so requests still succeed: `fallback: model-v2-small`. Patch is `PATCH /models/model-v2/config` — do this before purge.
Morgan: If we see a thundering herd during purge, abort purge and revert to TTL-only approach. Also keep DRI for Dedicated customers in the loop (they may have pinned sessions).
Eli: After rollback, schedule a post-mortem checklist item: identify root cause (sticky cookie attr? cache key change?) and add an automated canary-watch alert for KV miss-rate > 5% over 5m.
ops-bot: Canary rollback job rollback-1768501234 status: IN_PROGRESS (owner: Tom). Links: https://console.redwood.local/ops/rollback/rollback-1768501234
Aisha: Thanks — executing now. Ping here once KV purge starts and when split change completes. :thumbsup:
Tom: Split set to 0, baseline 100% — console shows green.
Kevin: Starting dry-run purge now, will remove --dry-run in next 60s if stable.
Eli: Quota & guard applied.
Morgan: Issued cookie expiry on edge; draining canary instances.
Aisha: Verified metrics trending down on KV misses. Good work team.
Tom: Leaving detailed steps in runbook under /runbooks/rollbacks/session-affinity-kv.md after we finish.
Aisha: Post-mortem to follow but rollback successful for now.
